2) Pilomatricoma — common in children/teens; typically a firm, solitary subcutaneous nodule.  
3) Lipoma — benign fatty tumor; usually soft and mobile but can present in adolescents.  
4) Dermatofibroma — small, firm, benign dermal nodule that can slowly enlarge.  
5) Vascular lesion (capillary hemangioma/venous malformation) — possible if lesion is compressible or has vascular features.

Rationale and plan (concise): The ranking is based on a solitary, gradually enlarging skin nodule over ~6 months in a 16-year-old with no known trigger. To confirm diagnosis and guide treatment I recommend a focused physical exam (document exact location, size, consistency, mobility, overlying skin changes) and a soft-tissue ultrasound to differentiate cystic vs solid and assess vascularity; definitive diagnosis usually requires excisional biopsy or removal with histology.
